drivers.name: Thanksgiving holiday (event week)
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted lift x1.12 from 2 past occurrences; 2025 outlier (x1.52) not representative.

adjustment.analysis: The Thanksgiving holiday is a strong driver with a noise-adjusted lift of x1.12 from two past occurrences, but the 2025 week (x1.52) was an outlier. The price increase to $4.56 (+5.1%) likely suppresses demand; recent week at same price (2026-09-28) saw 207 units (baseline 207.6), suggesting near-neutral effect. The TikTok trend is unverified and lacks historical support. No prior promotion at this price point. The classical model’s x1.12 is a reasonable starting point but overweights the holiday effect. Adjust downward due to price increase and weak evidence for TikTok. Median adjustment shrunk toward 1.0.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.2 - 290.6 | 10%-90%: 156.1 - 281.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
